column1: # no built HTML or XML file holds a numeric character reference to a code
# tools/sitecheck.py). html.parser decodes references with html.unescape,
# which drops those 94 code points (U+0001 to U+0008, U+000B, U+000E to
# U+001F, U+007F, U+FDD0 to U+FDEF and the two last code points of every
# plane), while the browser keeps them. So rel="stylesheet" is a
# stylesheet link to every rule that reads the page through html.parser
# (D9, (j), (k), (m), (a), (o), render) and none to the browser, and
#  after the CSP meta ends the head for the browser only. The rule
# reads the raw text, not a parser's reading, so it refuses such a
# reference anywhere: in text, in a quoted or unquoted value, in an
# attribute name, an end tag and raw text, where neither reading decodes
# (an over-refusal by design; the build writes no such reference). One
# row per reader of the issue, per spelling (hex with x or X and
# either case of digits, no ';', leading zeros), per range bound and its
# outer neighbour, per context, at the start and end of the file, a count
# row, look-alikes that are no reference in either reading, and the two
# XML files Page reads. Out-of-range references pass: both readings give
# U+FFFD. On a copy of render/pass-intake (the real built pages, no built
# pins) through site_intake_runner in tools/selftest.sh, label
# site-charref; the rows with the built pins on are in head-cases.tsv.
# Columns: name, file, find (exactly one occurrence), replace, expect (PASS
# or a text the findings must hold). The table holds only ASCII: \u{XXXX}
# in find and replace is that code point.
